Forgive me, my recipe book was my mother's last gift to me before she died. This recipe, and my mother as well, were always a little on the nebulous side. There are no measurements, just ballpark suggestions. This is one of the recipes that were so frequent in the family I doubt she even referenced a cookbook. You can tell that she simply sat down and imparted the recipes to me from memory.

East-West Rice

A few cups of day old rice
A couple strips of bacon
A couple scrambled eggs
A couple chopped green onions
A couple dashes of sesame oil
Ginger, either freshly grated or powdered (no amount given)
A Couple cloves of garlic

I've never noticed how vague this recipe must appear to an outsider until I went to share it. Bear with me.

Cook bacon and set aside, cook green onions, ginger and garlic briefly in bacon leavings, set aside (remove from pan) scramble eggs and set aside. add rice and more oil or bacon grease if necessary. When heated through, mix all together and add sesame oil, salt and pepper to taste.
